key_points.point: Net income fell from $3,314.6M (FY2023) to $1,635.3M (FY2024), down about 51%. Diluted EPS fell from $6.55 to $3.28 and basic EPS from $6.60 to $3.30.

The main driver was revenue, which fell about 23% from $12,305.5M to $9,427.2M. Cost of sales fell much less ($4,428.3M to $4,045.8M), so gross margin dropped from $7,877.2M to $5,381.3M (about 64% to 57% of revenue) and operating income fell from $3,823.1M to $2,032.8M.

Non-operating items added to the decline. Interest expense rose from $264.6M to $322.2M and Other, net swung from $8.2M of income to $12.0M of expense. Higher interest income ($78.8M vs $41.3M) partly offset this. Total non-operating expense rose from $215.1M to $255.5M, and pre-tax income fell from $3,608.0M to $1,777.3M.

Partial offsets: total operating expenses fell from $4,054.1M to $3,348.5M. R&D fell from $1,660.2M to $1,487.9M, SMG&A from $1,273.6M to $1,068.6M, amortization of intangibles from $959.6M to $754.8M and special charges from $160.7M to $37.3M. Total intangibles amortization in the cash flow statement also fell, from $1,958.4M to $1,741.5M. The tax provision fell from $293.4M to $142.1M, although the effective rate stayed about 8% in both years.

Period comparability: FY2024 was a 53-week year and FY2023 was a 52-week year. The extra week falls in the first quarter ended February 3, 2024. So FY2024 has one more week of operations, and the decline happened despite that extra week.

Debt balances at year end: long-term debt rose to $6,634.3M from $5,902.5M. Current debt fell to $399.6M from $499.1M. Commercial paper notes were roughly flat at $547.7M vs $547.2M. Total debt was about $7.58B vs about $6.95B.

New borrowing and repayments: in FY2024 the company raised $1,087.9M of debt and repaid $500.0M, which matches the roughly $499M of current debt at the end of FY2023. In FY2023 it raised no new debt and made no scheduled repayments; it only terminated $65.7M of debt early. The revolver was not used in either year (it was drawn and repaid $400M only in FY2022).

Commercial paper: in FY2024 the company issued $10,184.4M and repaid $10,183.9M, so net CP was flat and the balance stayed about $548M. In FY2023 it issued $5,287.1M and repaid $4,739.9M, a net addition of about $547M, which built the CP balance from nothing in FY2022.
Interest cost: interest expense rose to $322.2M in FY2024 from $264.6M in FY2023 ($200.4M in FY2022). Interest income rose to $78.8M from $41.3M.
Free cash flow: FY2024 operating cash flow of $3,852.5M minus capex of $730.5M gives about $3,122M. FY2023 operating cash flow of $4,817.6M minus capex of $1,261.5M gives about $3,556M.

Shareholder returns: FY2024 dividends of $1,795.5M ($3.62/share) plus buybacks of $615.6M total about $2,411M. FY2023 dividends of $1,679.1M ($3.34/share) plus buybacks of $2,964.0M total about $4,643M.

Coverage: in FY2024 free cash flow covered dividends and buybacks with a surplus of about $711M (about 1.3x). In FY2023 it fell short by about $1,087M (about 0.77x). The swing came mainly from much smaller buybacks and lower capex, even though operating cash flow was lower.

Where the FY2024 surplus went: together with net new term debt of about $588M ($1,087.9M raised minus $500.0M repaid; commercial paper net flat), it shows up as cash rising $1,033.3M to $1,991.3M and about $370M of net short-term investment purchases ($371.8M balance). Long-term debt rose to $6,634.3M.
How the FY2023 shortfall was funded: net commercial paper borrowing of about $547M ($5,287.1M issued minus $4,739.9M repaid) plus a $512.5M drawdown of cash, which fell from $1,470.6M to $958.1M.
